composition_mechanism.type: direct handoff x2 (stance->walk, then walk->lower), no scripted blend
composition_mechanism.description: Three SimHexapodJointWalkEnv instances, one per role's own exact recorded cfg-set (each role's bus.write_speed/safety.max_delta_q_deg/goal.joint_action_bias_* differ and are cached at env __init__, so one live env can't hot-swap them). At each handoff tick the raw physical state (qpos/qvel/ctrl/act + SafetyLayer._last_safe slew memory) is copied from the outgoing env into a freshly-reset incoming env (fresh plant-frame goal/tilt/height anchors via the established 'reanchor_keep_state' trick), then mj_forward + a rebuilt observation. No joint trajectory is scripted at either handoff.

CORROBORATION UPDATE (2026-10-01, lowerrole_overcurrent_stallclass_2026-10-01/SUMMARY.md): per audit_over_current.py's own operator-directed classification, only 5/37 (14%) of the raw over_current terminations in this sample are CORROBORATED_STALL (genuinely static joint + no body progress) -- the other 32/37 (86%, including most of L5 hip's share) are RAIL_MOVING (hot joint still turning / body still progressing), not corroborated as an unsafe stall by this test. The composed pass-rate numbers above are UNCHANGED (episodes still terminate early either way) -- this does not raise lower_ok -- but it narrows what a future mechanism should target: the genuine-stall subset is small and concentrated on L1 hip (4/5), a different joint than the raw per-joint tally implied, and s0 has ZERO corroborated stalls across both seed draws (further support for the s0-over-s1 seed choice above).
gate_summary.envelope_update_2026-10-02: The L1-hip genuine-stall mechanism flagged above is now CLOSED: `safety.hip_pitch_max_deg` was adopted as a model-source-derived SafetyLayer default (mesh/mesh_mjx -> 29.8deg, the CAD-true hip-pitch stop, vs the old uncapped-to-servo-range +40deg clip) -- a pure runtime inference-time filter, so this SAME s0 checkpoint (unmodified, no retrain) now runs under the corrected envelope automatically. Re-ran this entry's own composed gate protocol against it (zero GPU spend, pure re-eval): s0 **26/36** (72%, seed0 12/18 + seed100 14/18) and s1 **18/36** (50%, seed0 9/18 + seed100 9/18) -- both UNCHANGED/slightly BETTER than the old-clip numbers above, not worse, confirming the corrected envelope does not cost composed robustness. `trip_summary.stall_classification` on all 54 over_current traces (both seeds): 0 CORROBORATED_STALL, 100% RAIL_MOVING -- the L1-hip dead-zone exploit this checkpoint was already (accidentally) benefiting from under the old loose clip is now also gone for it, for free. A separate from-scratch SAC retrain under the new envelope (`hippitchmax-acq1-r2-cont1`) was tried as a vehicle for this fix and regressed hard (s0 7/36, s1 2/36) -- that regression is ordinary training-quality variance in that specific retrain, not a structural cost of the fix (see `lowerrole_drrampacq1_newclip_baseline_2026-10-02/SUMMARY.md`); no retrain is adopted or needed. The open gap narrows to: ~28% (s0) / ~50% (s1) of composed episodes still terminate on RAIL_MOVING over_current (not a corroborated stall, i.e. the joint is working, just hot/high-current) -- a policy control-quality question, not a safety-envelope or stall-exploit one. system-ID follow-up the same day (walkcurr STATUS Next 1) further rules out recalibrating the current trip threshold as the fix (a scripted open-loop baseline stays <=43% of rail at every trained depth) -- any future mechanism must improve the policy's own current usage, not the limit or the envelope.
